subject: chemistry
title: Greenhouse Effect & Climate Change
welcome_lead: A blanket of gases keeps Earth warm. Too thick a blanket and the planet overheats.
meta_desc: Understand the greenhouse effect and climate change in this KS3 chemistry adventure.
final_note: You can now explain why our climate is changing and what we can do.

concepts.def: Gases trap heat that would otherwise escape to space.
Gas that traps heat: e.g. CO₂, methane, water vapour.
Coal, oil, gas; burning them releases CO₂.
Long-term changes in temperature and weather patterns.
Energy source that does not run out, e.g. solar, wind.
Total CO₂ produced by a person or activity.

walkthroughs.body_html: Sunlight warms Earth's surface. Some heat is reflected back, but greenhouse gases like CO₂, methane and water vapour trap some of it. Without this effect, Earth would be frozen.

walkthroughs.h2: Too much of a good thing
walkthroughs.body_html:
Burning fossil fuels adds extra CO₂ to the atmosphere. The blanket gets thicker, so the planet warms more than it should.

More CO₂ = more warming.
Warmer temperatures lead to melting ice caps, rising sea levels and more extreme weather. We can reduce CO₂ by using renewables, planting trees and saving energy.

mcqs.q: Is the oxidation state of an atom the same as its actual charge?
options: Not necessarily — oxidation state is an accounting tool assuming all bonds are fully ionic; real charge is usually smaller.
The oxidation state of an atom is always equal to the number of electrons it has.
The oxidation state of an atom is exactly equal to its real ionic charge in every compound.
The forward reaction stops once the reverse reaction begins.

mcqs.q: What is reduction in terms of electrons?
options: Reduction means losing oxygen and oxidation means gaining oxygen — full stop.
Reduction means a substance becomes physically smaller in size.
Gain of electrons (the oxidation number is reduced).
The oxidation state of an atom is always equal to the number of electrons it has.
